source.title: Scaling Behavior of Machine Translation with Large Language Models under Prompt Injection Attacks
source.authors: Zhi-Fan Sun; Antonio Valerio Miceli Barone

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream task performance across model sizes in a multilingual machine-translation setting and reports cases of inverse or non-monotonic scaling, qualifying the claim that downstream performance improves predictably with scale.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates translation accuracy across model sizes on clean and prompt-injection examples. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, extrapolate loss, or find compute-optimal allocations. Attack-condition findings concern behavior elicited by an injected instruction and are not evidence about uninduced downstream performance.
record.test_reason: On clean (non-attacked) translation inputs, the study compares task accuracy across model sizes in six model families. That bears directly on V6, and some settings show non-monotonic or inverse scaling. It does not measure pretraining loss, fit power laws or study allocation, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors find positive or flat scaling with size on clean examples for most families. They find inverse or non-monotonic scaling under prompt injection, especially zero-shot, and zero-shot Llama2 shows inverse scaling even on clean examples. One in-context example, instruction tuning or code pretraining can mitigate this. English-source questions act as stronger distractors, which they describe as inverse scaling w.r.t. training data but cannot quantify as a scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: Measures question-mark accuracy and BLEU on prompt-based translation across existing model sizes; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit the original scaling-law models.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported trends vary with model family, language direction, zero-shot versus one-shot prompting, clean versus adversarial input, and quantization. The paper also cautions that English-to-X zero-shot Llama2 accuracy may reflect repeating the English source rather than translating.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the prompt-injection attack, GPT-3/InstructGPT show inverse scaling for En→De and En→Fr, Llama2 zero-shot shows inverse scaling, and Llama2-chat shows U-shaped scaling. The GPT-3.5 models reverse the trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Susceptibility to instruction-injection distractors grows with model size (inverse scaling) unless the model is instruction- or code-trained.

fits_no_version.finding: Models answer rather than translate more often when the source is English (Table 2: X→En 0.90–0.93 clean vs En→X 0.71–0.75). The authors call this inverse scaling w.r.t. training data size but do not measure data size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distractor strength rises with the model's familiarity with the source language.

record.problems: The main accuracy measure is a coarse question-mark heuristic; the authors acknowledge that failed translations may still end with question marks. Many results are presented in plots without tabulated values. The study covers a limited number of model families and one prompt-injection setting, and it does not quantify training-corpus sizes or language proportions.
record.rows_left_out: Adversarial prompt-injection scaling curves and corresponding BLEU plots are not recorded as rows because the attack instruction deliberately elicits answering rather than translating; those results do not measure uninduced downstream performance for V6. Appendix C BLEU curves are also omitted because the text does not state their individual values or describe most individual trends.

untested.parts: Tasks other than prompt-based translation of questions. The link between downstream performance and pretraining loss. Any quantitative fit or prediction of the scaling curve: only the direction of trends is reported, from plots.

missing.what: Llama2 one-shot clean BLEU: positive scaling with size
Llama2 4-bit quantized clean zero-shot: abrupt increase then steady decrease in accuracy with size
Llama2-chat one-shot clean: performs less well than zero-shot; scaling trend not stated

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is figure-only and uses a coarse question-mark heuristic. There are few sizes per family (3–4) and no uncertainty is reported. Adversarial results are correctly excluded from V6, since the attack induces the failure on purpose. Predictability is judged only qualitatively (trend direction), not as a fitted law.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger-run loss from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, and its scaling with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests translation accuracy across model sizes, but not performance on other downstream tasks or its relationship to pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices or estimate exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: GPT-3
rows.operation_detail: Compared translation performance across model sizes.
rows.note: The text reports two drops, from 350M to 1.3B and from 6.7B to 175B, but says these are insignificant relative to the overall rise from 1.3B to 175B.
rows.check: Authors call the two drops insignificant next to the overall 1.3B→175B rise and say it is not inverse scaling. 'Partial' is borderline; 'observed' is also defensible.

rows.subject: Llama2
rows.operation_detail: Compared translation performance across model sizes.

conditions.value: X-to-English; the paper identifies these as valid examples
not specified for this stated trend

rows.note: The authors describe obvious inverse scaling in zero-shot Llama2. They caution that high accuracy in English-to-X can reflect English repetition rather than translation.
rows.check: Locator and condition are fine. The 'valid X-to-English' caveat comes from Sec. 3.2 (adversarial). For clean inputs, Sec. 3.1 says English-to-X zero-shot accuracy reflects English repetition (BLEU <10), not translation. Only three sizes (7B/13B/70B). Quantization variants are mixed in, and the 4-bit variant behaves differently.

rows.subject: Llama2
rows.operation_detail: Compared translation performance across model sizes.
rows.note: The text reports near-perfect accuracy with flat or slightly inverse scaling; it separately reports positive scaling in BLEU scores.
rows.check: Question-mark accuracy is at ceiling ('near perfect'), so this measure cannot show improvement with size. The text reports positive BLEU scaling in the same setting, but no row records it (see missing).

rows.subject: Llama2-chat
rows.operation_detail: Compared translation performance across model sizes.
rows.note: The authors report positive scaling for Llama2-chat in zero-shot mode.

relationships.condition: Clean inputs: T5 En→Fr/Ro, FLAN-T5 all pairs, GPT-3 except En→Fr, InstructGPT, Llama2-chat zero-shot, Llama2 one-shot in BLEU
relationships.reason: Authors report positive, almost monotonic scaling in these settings (r2, r3, r5, r6, r9). Llama2 one-shot BLEU also scales positively per the text (Sec. 3.1), not yet a row.
relationships.display_finding: On clean inputs, translation performance scales positively and almost monotonically for T5 English-to-French and English-to-Romanian, all tested FLAN-T5 pairs, GPT-3 except English-to-French, InstructGPT and zero-shot Llama2-chat, while one-shot Llama2 BLEU also scales positively.

relationships.condition: Clean inputs: T5 En→De; GPT-3 En→Fr; Llama2 4-bit quantized
relationships.reason: T5 En→De shows U-shaped scaling (r1). GPT-3 En→Fr dips twice, though authors deem the dips insignificant (r4). Per text, 4-bit Llama2 rises then steadily declines (not a row).
relationships.display_finding: T5 English-to-German performance was U-shaped, GPT-3 English-to-French had two dips deemed insignificant, and 4-bit Llama2 improved initially before steadily declining.

relationships.condition: Clean inputs, Llama2 pretrained, zero-shot, X-to-English directions
relationships.reason: Authors report 'quite obvious inverse scaling' across 7B–70B on non-adversarial examples (r7).
relationships.display_finding: Translation performance declined across 7B–70B even on non-adversarial examples.
